title: fastpath-emission-adoption-smokeplan-and-rewind-procedure
body:
Overview:

This is a working draft for onboarding the "fast-path emission" (lookahead/early-token emission) runtime path for new models and kernel combos. Goal is to provide a concise smoke-test plan, clear telemetry thresholds, and an operational "rewind" (rollback) procedure that SRE/infra can run with minimal coordination. Not prescriptive for permanent rollout decisions — this is a safe, repeatable acceptance + evacuation plan.

High-level intent:
- Validate correctness (no hallucinated prefix duplication, KV coherence).
- Validate stability (no sudden p95 spikes, no new OOM patterns).
- Validate economic impact (token throughput, per-token cost delta).
- Provide fast abort/rewind path that restores previous kernel/model variant and clears any cached state that could cause stale outputs.

Assumptions and scope:
- Applies to: emission fast-path layer that uses anticipatory token generation, new kernel routing heuristics, and KV-cache speculative writes.
- Excludes changes to client API surface, function-calling semantics, and long-tail model weights.
- Runs in dedicated canary pool initially (3 nodes, mixed GPU types).

Quick summary checklist (smoke):
- Launch canary deployment targeting 5% of requests for a single model-version.
- Run a synthetic suite: short prompts (<=64 tokens), medium (256), long (>1024) including repeated-prefix stress cases.
- Validate KV hit-rate baseline vs control.
- Run 500 concurrent steady-stream connections; verify p50/p95, error-rate below thresholds.
- Run regression prompts from golden promptset (see linked_artifacts).

Metrics and thresholds (immediate abort triggers):
- latency_p50_ms: no more than +15% vs control; alert if +30%.
- latency_p95_ms: no more than +25% vs control; auto-abort if +50% sustained for >5m.
- error_rate_per_minute: must remain < 0.5% (if >= 1% -> immediate rollback).
- kv_write_failure_rate: any non-zero spike >0.1% sustained over 2m -> investigate and consider rollback.
- kv_effective_hit_rate: should not drop >5 percentage points relative to baseline for same workload.
- token_duplication_rate: <0.01% false duplicates (dedupe check in smoke harness).
- token_cost_per_k: target delta within ±12% for same prompt mix; >20% increase => abort.

Telemetry keys (examples):
- runtime.fastpath.emission.attempts, .success, .fallbacks
- runtime.kernel.route.latency_ms.{kernel_id}
- runtime.kv.write.latency_ms, .hit, .miss
- request.trace.fastpath.enabled (boolean per-request)

Smoke harness (practical):
- Use bench/emission-smoke harness (repo: serving-runtime/tools/bench).
- Config: mix = {short:40%, med:40%, long:20%}, concurrency 500, duration 15m per run.
- Harness should post results to a temporary dashboard (grafana temp id, see linked_artifacts).
- Harness also runs a golden-prompt diff: compare control output vs fastpath output token-by-token; tolerate allowed variability config (top-k sampling differences), but flag structural mismatches (missing tokens, duplicated prefixes, truncated output).

Kernel scheduling knobs to watch:
- early_emit_threshold_tokens: nominal 2-4 tokens (reduce high false early-emits).
- kernel_route_timeout_ms: 30ms (if exceeded, immediate fallback to safe kernel).
- continuous_batch_window_ms: small increases reduce throughput variance but increase tail latency — measure p95 impact.
- kv_commit_mode: async vs sync (smoke should test sync for correctness then async for perf).

KV-cache coherence & probes:
- Every speculative write tagged with request_id + speculative_seq; on fallback/rollback, we must garbage-collect by request_id.
- Run consistency probe: issue controlled sequence (A->B->A) and verify KV returns expected prefix snapshots.
- Probe pattern: 1000 short sequences with random interleaving; track any out-of-order or stale reads. Abort if >0.05% failures.

Canary rollout plan (recommended):
- Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local replay harness (done before this doc).
- Phase 1 (canary small): 5% traffic, 3 nodes, 1 hour smoke runs every 30m. Manual sign-off by eng on-call and SRE.
- Phase 2 (canary expand): 20% traffic, mixed-region, 6 hours sustained. Automated checks; if any abort triggers, auto rewind.
- Phase 3 (ramp): 50%+ over 48 hours with continuous monitoring and customer-traffic segregation. Final decision after 72h.

Rewind/rollback procedure ("rewind" because of KV state):
- Goal: return serving pool to pre-fastpath state and clean any speculative KV state.
- Steps (manual or automated runbook):
  1) Switch routing: update routing policy to send 100% traffic to control variant (api call: POST /route/update {model,variant:control}).
  2) Quiesce fastpath instances: drain connections from fastpath pool (k8s: kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/fastpath-<canary>). Wait for in-flight requests to finish (grace period 60s).
  3) Clear speculative KV entries: run kv-gc tool with --prefix=speculative:request_id:* (tool logs to S3, dry-run first). In heavy production, use per-request tombstones to avoid race.
  4) Revert kernels: redeploy previous kernel image tag (CI artifact) to canary nodes (kubectl set image...).
  5) Validate: run quick smoke (30m low-concurrency) to confirm p95/p50 back to baseline and kv hit rates recovered.
  6) Postmortem: create postmortem doc within 48h, include all metrics and a timeline.

Automated abort logic (for SRE runbooks):
- If any abort trigger fires, an automated job should:
  - Post Slack alert to #infra-alerts with category "fastpath-abort"
  - Run step 1 (routing switch) and step 3 (kv-gc dry-run) automatically.
  - Tag the canary instance with reason for rollback (metadata) for debugging.
- Note: fully destructive gc (step 3 final) should require manual approval in case of false positives.

Manual verification checklist (SRE/eng on-call):
- Pull recent traces for a sample user request and verify token ordering.
- Confirm no increase in client retries (look at API gateway logs).
- Validate cost metrics in billing-realtime: per-token cost delta.
- Run additional golden prompts that previously failed in historical replays.

Edge cases and failure modes to watch:
- Back-to-back fallback thrash: workload that repeatedly trips fastpath and falls back causing twice the compute. Add cooldown per-request.
- KV lineage leak: speculative writes not tombstoned due to partial failure of gc job. Add idempotent tombstones.
- OOM patterns: fastpath can change memory KPIs; have emergency pod eviction threshold lower for canary.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define deterministic dedupe algorithm for near-identical outputs (Rina to propose by 2025-03-10).
- Decide whether kv speculative writes should be retained for N seconds after fallback for debugging (privacy and cost tradeoff).
- Confirm ownership of automated rollback job (SRE vs infra-team).

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Route update: curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/routes -d '{"model":"mX","variant":"control"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
- Drain deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-controlplane && kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/fastpath-canary
- KV GC dry-run: /bin/kv-gc --mode=dry-run --match=speculative:* --report=/tmp/kv-gc-report.json
- Bench harness: serving-runtime/tools/bench/run_emission_smoke --config=smoke-large.json

Notes to self: keep the smoke harness config small and repeatable. Ask solutions-eng for a customer-realistic prompt set before Phase 2. This doc is intentionally lightweight — aim to convert into a Confluence playbook after two successful canaries.
